result.topic_en: Problem V: determining the vibratory motions of an elastic lamina clamped (fixed in an immovable wall) at both ends, setting up the four boundary equations and deriving two expressions for the ratio C/D.
result.transcription:
LAMINARVM ELASTICARVM. 481
ſtylo defixum, vti terminus ſtylo defixus, ſe habet
ad terminum muro infixum.
Problema V.
Si lamina vtroque termino A $a$ et B $b$ fuerit muro immobili infixa, definire motus vibratorios quos recipere poterit.
Tab. VII. Fig. 8.
Solutio.
Poſita vt ante longitudine laminae $AB = a$, pro eius curuatura ſemper eadem aequatio valebit, qua hactenus ſumus vſi, ac pro hoc caſu ſolutio ſatis expedite euolui poteſt, propterea quod pro vtroque termino A et B, eſt tam $y = 0$, quam $(\frac{dy}{dx}) = 0$ hincque ſequentes quatuor aequationes obtinentur:
$\text{I. } A + C + D = 0$
$\text{II. } B + C - D = 0$
$\text{III. } A\,\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta + B\,\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta + Ce^{\zeta} + De^{-\zeta} = 0$
$\text{IV. } -A\,\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta + B\,\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta + Ce^{\zeta} - De^{-\zeta} = 0$
quarum $\text{III.}\,\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta - \text{IV.}\,\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta$ praebet
$A = Ce^{\zeta}(\mathrm{fin}\,\zeta - \mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta) - De^{-\zeta}(\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta + \mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta)$
$= -C - D$, vnde $\frac{C}{D} = \frac{e^{-\zeta}(\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta + \mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta) - 1}{e^{\zeta}(\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta - \mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta) + 1}$; ſimili modo
$\text{III.}\,\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta + \text{IV.}\,\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta$ dat
$B = -Ce^{\zeta}(\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta + \mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta) - De^{-\zeta}(\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta - \mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta)$
$= -C + D$, vnde $\frac{C}{D} = \frac{e^{-\zeta}(\mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta - \mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta) + 1}{-e^{\zeta}(\mathrm{cof.}\,\zeta + \mathrm{fin.}\,\zeta) + 1}$
Tom. XVII. Nou. Comm. Ppp qui

items.english: If the lamina is fixed in an immovable wall at both ends Aa and Bb, to determine the vibratory motions which it can receive.

items.english: In this case the solution can be worked out quite readily, because at both ends A and B we have both y = 0 and dy/dx = 0.
